# core/blake2s.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/blake2s.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

BLAKE2s (RFC 7693) and HMAC-BLAKE2s (RFC 2104 over it).

What is proved: every access is in bounds, nothing leaks, and a digest is
as long as asked for (1 to 32 bytes). Not proved: that the digest is
BLAKE2s's (the tests check the RFC 7693 vectors, a keyed hash, and the
lengths around a block), or that the code takes the same time for every
input (it does not branch on its data, but nothing checks that).
WireGuard uses both: the hash, the 16-byte keyed hash as its MAC, and the
HMAC for its key derivation.

`import "core/blake2s.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/endian.bastio](core-endian.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`blake2s`](#blake2s) | The BLAKE2s digest of `m` under `key` (empty for none, at most 32 bytes), `outlen` bytes long (1 to 32). |
| [`hmac_blake2s`](#hmac_blake2s) | HMAC-BLAKE2s-256 of `msg` under `key` (any length). |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `blake2s`

```bastio
fn blake2s(m: &Bytes, key: &Bytes, outlen: u64) -> Bytes
  requires outlen >= 1 && outlen <= 32 && blen(key) <= 32 && blen(m) <= 576460752303423488
  ensures blen(result) == outlen
```

The BLAKE2s digest of `m` under `key` (empty for none, at most 32 bytes),
`outlen` bytes long (1 to 32). A key or length out of range gives a
32-byte digest of nothing: callers check first.

Example:

```bastio
let m = bfrom("abc");
let k = balloc(0);
let d = blake2s(m, k, 32);
let first = bget(d, 0);          // 50 8c 5e 8c ... 82
let last = bget(d, 31);
bfree(d);
bfree(k);
bfree(m);
if first != 80 || last != 130 { return 1; }
```

### `hmac_blake2s`

```bastio
fn hmac_blake2s(key: &Bytes, msg: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(msg) <= 288230376151711744 && blen(key) <= 288230376151711744
  ensures blen(result) == 32
```

HMAC-BLAKE2s-256 of `msg` under `key` (any length): 32 bytes. WireGuard's
key derivation is built on this (block size 64).

Example:

```bastio
let key = bfrom("key");
let msg = bfrom("msg");
let mac = hmac_blake2s(key, msg);
let n = blen(mac);
bfree(mac);
bfree(key);
bfree(msg);
if n != 32 { return 1; }
```

## Internals

### `blake2s_sigma`

```bastio
fn blake2s_sigma() -> Vec[u32]
  ensures vlen(result) == 160
```

Internal: the message word order of the ten rounds, 16 words each.

### `blake2s_iv`

```bastio
fn blake2s_iv() -> Vec[u32]
  ensures vlen(result) == 8
```

Internal: the initial state, SHA-256's.

### `blake2s_rotr`

```bastio
fn blake2s_rotr(x: u32, n: u64) -> u32
  requires n >= 1 && n <= 31
```

Internal: `x` rotated right by `n` bits, 1 to 31.

### `blake2s_g`

```bastio
fn blake2s_g(v: &mut Vec[u32], a: u64, b: u64, c: u64, d: u64, x: u32, y: u32)
  requires vlen(v) == 16 && a < 16 && b < 16 && c < 16 && d < 16
  ensures vlen(v) == 16
```

Internal: the mixing function G on words a, b, c, d of v.

### `blake2s_block`

```bastio
fn blake2s_block(h: &mut Vec[u32], iv: &Vec[u32], sigma: &Vec[u32], m: &Bytes, at: u64, t: u64, last: bool)
  requires vlen(h) == 8 && vlen(iv) == 8 && vlen(sigma) == 160 && at + 64 <= blen(m)
  ensures vlen(h) == 8
```

Internal: the state after the 64-byte block at `at` of `m`; `t` bytes
have been hashed once it is counted, and `last` marks the final block.
